tp4-mtp.rationale: GLM's accepted arm is a fresh capture of the GATES4 install at 8c75e90bd, the adopted qualification's part B, one per policy. Margins from GLM's own same-build neutral evidence (accepted DCP 1 against DCP 2, DCP 4 and BF16 KV; 35 texts, 3,781 positions): pooled upper clustered CI95 at most 0.005 nats mean error (DCP 2 reached 0.0040), category mean point increase at most 0.015 nats (1.4 times the largest observed, BF16 KV chat +0.0107), pooled net top-one upper CI95 at most 0.01, and at most four net positions whose absolute error grows by more than 0.5 nats (DCP 2's +3 plus one). Holm alpha 0.05, the eight-text CI minimum and sparse pooled refusal are unchanged. DCP 2 and 4 have their own accepted arms. Operator approved the accepted arm and these margins on 2026-10-11; two independent accepted captures per policy are calibrated before the pins are filled.

limitations: glm5next's default configuration is qualified: the operator adopted its GATES4 results on 2026-10-11 (part A, the autoregressive arms, at cab96b599; part B at 8c75e90bd), its soak judged after the declared warm-up stated below. The checkpoint identity is the one the engine reported for the zai-org FP8 checkpoint at its pinned revision (startup serving_identity of a TP4 tp4-mtp serve, 2026-10-07). The teacher, long-context and image-probe references are adopted (models/glm5next/reference.py, step 30) and pin repository, revision, served model name and source lock.

This declaration qualifies the default configuration alone (tp4-mtp: TP4, FP8 latent KV, DCP 1), one gate run against one server: every live check and record requires context_parallel_size 1, TP4 and FP8 KV. DCP 2 and 4, BF16 latent KV and encoder parity, which needs the diagnostic-taps build, are qualified by their own configurations (configurations.dcp2, dcp4, kv-bf16 and taps in this file), each gated against its own server, since a TP4 server takes all four GPUs.

Determinism compares two records of tools/qual/determinism.py record --server-log, each bound to the pinned checkpoint and the live process that answered it: determinism_ar from an autoregressive server and determinism_spec from an MTP one (both with --image: this declaration claims image input, so each record must include the image request). The gate scores the MTP record against the AR record (reference_file), which must share its run ID, checkpoint and build (package identity, version, source commit; reference_equal), so speculative output must equal AR bit for bit, as must each record's cold repeat and prefix hits.

This run records the FP8 arms later paired runs compare against, each bound to this server's identity: the full cohort's teacher writes its capture to {raw}/teacher-capture.json beside its receipt (the FP8 arm of the kv-bf16 configuration's teacher_arms), and evals_gsm8k answers the whole GSM8K test split as arm fp8 under this run's ID, bound to the pinned checkpoint and this server's startup log (the FP8 arm of each NVFP4 declaration's paired GSM8K).

paired_teacher compares this server's teacher capture (the candidate arm) with the stored accepted arm of the same configuration and arm: the correctness runner reads stored_teacher from each of its stores (last good and seed, both seeded with the accepted captures of the GATES4 install at 8c75e90bd, served the same way) and reports a store without one as no baseline yet (tools/qual/README.md#correctness-runner, docs/paired-accuracy.md). Its margins are tp4-mtp's, which the operator approved on 2026-10-11 (0.005 nats pooled, 0.015 per category, 0.01 top-one, four tail positions); each configuration that declares the check (both DCP sizes, both NVFP4 checkpoints) selects them by its profile, on its own teacher reference. No margins are declared for tp4-ar, which no GLM gate run serves; it is tied to tp4-mtp by the bit-for-bit determinism pair and the AR-versus-MTP spec_verify and verify_exact pairs.

The soak's memory rule declares a warm-up and a cache allowance (operator, 2026-10-11; soak.memory_rule): a request's last prompt chunk (at most 64 rows) captures its prefill program at its first run and keeps it, at most 64 lengths (models/glm5next/README.md, Qualification checks), each about 40 MiB host and 21 MiB GPU across the four ranks. Growth after the first 180 s must stay within 512 MiB host and GPU, and growth over the whole soak within 512 MiB plus the 64 programs' bound (2,560 MiB host, 1,344 MiB GPU). In GATES4 (8c75e90bd, 2026-10-11) the DCP 1 soak grew 1,077.5 MiB host over its 1,380 s and 43.6 MiB after 180 s; the local-inference-lab NVFP4 gate's soak 529.2 and 48.1 MiB; the NVIDIA NVFP4 gate's 480.0 and 43.3 MiB. GPU memory for all 64 programs is left: every GATES4 server had at least 989 MiB free per rank before its first graph capture, and all 64 programs with every other graph take at most about 500 MiB per rank. The full soak runs 1,200 s so that its job fits the release preview's 1,740-second bound.

chat scores the chat reference (fixtures/glm5next/chat-reference.json: the seven teacher chat texts and ten longer conversations of 251 to 603 tokens, 4,340 positions, eleven of the seventeen crossing four 64-token pages) teacher-forced like the teacher check, with the spread rule's mean headroom factor 1.25 (SPREAD_MEAN_FACTOR, adopted 2026-10-11, fixed before the references ran). Its limits come from the reference alone: BF16 spread 0.180 mean, 3.1% decisive, 6.4% total; f64 0.014. So the mean limit is 0.25 (1.25 x 0.180 rounded up to 0.05) and the top-1 limits are the floors (8%, 8%, 10%). The teacher check keeps its seven chat texts and limits. The full cohort's capture ({raw}/chat-capture.json) is the arm a paired comparison reads; the quick cohort writes none, so chopinfer eval captures both quick checks.

frontend_goldens captures the served frontend itself (--url): each row of fixtures/glm5next/frontend/chat-renders.json, which transformers 5.16.1 rendered from the pinned revision's chat_template.jinja and tokenized with its tokenizer.json on CPU (models/glm5next/compiler/fixtures/checkpoints/glm-5.3-flash/goldens.py --gate; no vLLM capture), goes to /tokenize, as does each text of the tokenizer goldens beside goldens.py, and the served token IDs must equal HF's. The rows cover the role tags, reasoning, reasoning_effort low, high and max, tool definitions, tool calls with non-string arguments and tool results, and the chat teacher conversations; images are left to media_preprocessing. It passed against served tp4-mtp, tp4-mtp-nvfp4 and tp4-mtp-nvfp4-nvidia servers (2026-10-11: 31 chat rows and 27 tokenizer rows, every token ID equal).

needle sends the frozen needle prompts (fixtures/glm5next/capture/needles.py: MiMo's functional haystack and three needles rebuilt in GLM's template as prompts of 7,168, 130,048 and 261,120 tokens with reasoning effort Low and 1,024 tokens to answer, total contexts of 8,192, 131,072 and 262,144; inputs.needle under $CHOPINFER_DATA, digests in fixtures/glm5next/needles.json) and requires the three values in order (alphanumeric match). 262,144 is the largest context: tp4-mtp's measured KV pool with images holds 442,112 tokens at 32 slots, so a 1,048,576-token context does not fit one sequence on the default package. The served tp4-mtp reports max_model_len 429,120. The needle passed at all three lengths against tp4-mtp at DCP 1, 2 and 4 and both NVFP4 exports (2026-10-11).

Not declared: a paired margin between the FP8 and BF16 KV arms (the kv-bf16 configuration's teacher_arms reports their difference; paired_teacher declares no BF16 KV policy), logprobs_parity, which compares the logprobs a reference OpenAI server returns with the candidate's: GLM's reference is HF transformers through tools/refrun, not a server, and the teacher, chat and long_context checks already score the served logprobs against it, while api covers the response shape; and video, which the bundle refuses. The long-context reference holds 131,072 tokens (long_128k); 262,144 does not fit one GPU job of the reference runner (models/glm5next/README.md).

api uses MiMo's API sample and tools-00 conversation (fixtures/mimo26), as the api check reads only their response shape and tool request; spec_verify uses MiMo's prompts and GSM8K questions as Qwen's does.

Release prerequisites outside this declaration (plan step 39, default config), recorded separately: kernel-lab reports for each GLM engine, and bring-up (chopinfer verify --model, a smoke test and the release preview's GSM8K screen at preview.gsm8k_floor, 193 of 200, the floor the operator adopted on 2026-10-11). spec_verify's GSM8K questions are prompts, not that screen.
